learn.title: Files are bytes
learn.body: A file is just bytes on disk. A text file holds bytes that stand for letters. Other files, such as images, hold bytes with other meanings. Opening with `"rb"` or `"wb"` treats a file as raw bytes, with no changes. `fread` and `fwrite` move blocks of them.

learn.title: Write and read bytes
learn.body: The program writes 4 bytes, then reads them back. It prints `4 bytes: 42 4d 00 ff`. `fwrite(buffer, size, count, f)` returns how many items were handled. Checks for `NULL` are left out here to fit.

learn.title: What an image file is
learn.body: An image is also bytes, and many formats begin with a signature that identifies them. A BMP file starts with the bytes 42 4D, which are the letters B and M. A PNG file starts with 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A, where 50 4E 47 spell PNG.

learn.title: Copying any file
learn.body: Reading one byte at a time with `fgetc` and writing it with `fputc` copies any file, including an image. This prints `copied 4` for the 4-byte file. `fgetc` returns an `int` so that it can also return `EOF`.

learn.title: Checking a signature
learn.body: The first two bytes you read are 42 and 4D.
steps: The file begins with BM, so it could be a BMP image

learn.body: Use "rb" and "wb" for anything that is not plain text. On some systems text mode changes line endings, which would damage an image.

questions.prompt: Which mode opens a file to write raw bytes?
How many bytes did the example program write and read back?
The byte 0x42 is the letter B. What is the hex byte 0x4D as a letter?
questions.explanation: 0x4D is 77 in decimal, the letter M.

questions.prompt: What do the first bytes of a BMP file spell?
questions.explanation: A BMP starts with 42 4D, the letters B and M.

questions.prompt: `fgetc` returns an \_\_ so it can also return `EOF`.
questions.explanation: An `int` can hold every byte value plus the special `EOF`.

questions.prompt: What does the copy loop do?
choices: Copies a file byte by byte
questions.explanation: It reads each byte and writes it unchanged to the other file.
